color_semantics.black_ink: Exact overlapping ink present in both scan and rebuilt page
color_semantics.red_ink: Scan ink only (original raster artifacts, scan paper defects, or un-reproduced scan text)
color_semantics.cyan_ink: Rebuilt ink only (vector digital type rendered by compiler)

redshift_and_coverage_explanation.does_it_completely_cover: No, not in the reflowed monograph edition by design. The monograph edition is reflowed (375 pages vs 341 scan pages) using modern Springer-style proportions (6.14x9.21 in, 10pt text), so lines break at different points and text flows independently of scan raster coordinates. Complete pixel-on-pixel coverage (1:1 spatial overlay where cyan sits directly on red) is only achieved in facsimile editions where every word bounding box is anchored to its original scan ink coordinates.

facsimile_coverage_results.page_alignment: 341 rebuilt pages = 341 source scan pages (1:1 page map)
facsimile_coverage_results.vertical_layout_pitch_error: 0.0 pt baseline shift on standard body columns

optical_redshift_semantics.black_ink: Exact overlapping ink where digital vector characters coincide with scan ink
optical_redshift_semantics.red_ink: Scan ink only (original lead-type ink bleed, paper texture, raster grain, scan dust, and scan diagram lines)
optical_redshift_semantics.cyan_ink: Rebuilt ink only (digital vector font outline curves outside the scan ink boundary)

facsimile_coverage_results.why_100_percent_pixel_overlap_is_bounded: 100% exact pixel match is physically impossible between an analog paper scan and a modern digital vector font: 1) Font Outline Variance: Songti SC OpenType outlines have different serif curves and stroke thicknesses compared to the 1990s metal/phototypesetting lead type, creating 1-2px edge fringes. 2) Paper Noise & Bleed: The scan contains raster scan noise and ink bleed (pure red) that digital vectors do not replicate. 3) The facsimile places 100% of recognized words directly inside their detected bounding boxes with 0 missing transcript lines.
